coupling_random_walk_keyword_matches.title: Sharp Lichnerowicz theorem
coupling_random_walk_keyword_matches.statement: For the $\varepsilon$-step random walk on an $N$-dimensional Riemannian manifold, the coarse-curvature argument gives the lower spectral-gap estimate $\inf\operatorname{Ric}$, whereas the sharp Lichnerowicz estimate is $\frac{N}{N-1}\inf\operatorname{Ric}$. Can the missing directional information be incorporated, for example through reflection couplings, to recover the sharp theorem?

coupling_random_walk_keyword_matches.title: Exact coupling of singular non-discrete random walks
coupling_random_walk_keyword_matches.statement: Let $S$ and $S'$ be random walks on $\mathbb{R}$ with the same i.i.d. step-length distribution, starting at $0$ and $x$. Suppose the step lengths are neither discrete nor spread out. For which initial positions $x$ can the walks be coupled so that $S_n=S'_n$ for every sufficiently large $n$ almost surely?
